name: NDA & NA
fullName: UPSC National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination
nameHi: राष्ट्रीय रक्षा अकादमी एवं नौसेना अकादमी परीक्षा
frequency: Twice a year (NDA I and NDA II)
approxCandidates: ≈4–6 lakh applicants per cycle (approx.); about 400 vacancies per cycle
eligibility: Unmarried candidates aged 16½–19½ who have passed or are appearing in Class 12; Physics, Chemistry and Maths required for the Air Force, Navy and Naval Academy wings

notification.summary: NDA & NA (II) 2026 was held on 13 September 2026, and its written result is expected in October 2026. Per UPSC's Calendar 2027, the NDA & NA (I) 2027 notification is due on 2 December 2026 and the exam on 11 April 2027. Dates are provisional; upsc.gov.in itself could not be reached from the research sandbox.

pattern.notes: There are two papers of 2½ hours each: Mathematics (120 questions × 2.5 marks) and the General Ability Test (150 questions × 4 marks; English 200 marks and GK 400 marks). Every wrong answer costs one-third of the question's marks, so the top-level 'marking' block gives the Maths values and each section carries its own 'marking'. The written test is followed by a 900-mark SSB interview. The bank holds 60 items in proportion (Maths 26, English 10, GK 24), so a short mock should be scored per section.

trendAnalysis.summary: The Maths paper is long and moderately tough. Algebra (complex numbers, quadratics, sequences, binomial, permutations and combinations) plus Calculus together give about 45% of it, and Statistics & Probability has grown recently. Time management, not concepts, is the main hurdle with 120 questions in 150 minutes. GAT English is easy to moderate and vocabulary-heavy (synonyms, antonyms, error spotting, comprehension). GAT GK is broad: Physics carries the most science weight, followed by History/Freedom Movement and Geography, with growing current-affairs and defence coverage. Overall difficulty has been stable over 2024–26, and Maths is the deciding paper.

resources.notes: UPSC posts NDA question papers on upsc.gov.in (Previous Question Papers) after each exam. Official answer keys appear only after the final result of that cycle.

pyqBlueprint.method: Built from the official NDA & NA (I) and (II) question papers that UPSC publishes, and from post-exam topic-wise analyses (Careers360, SSBCrack, Doon Defence Dreamers, Target Classes) for 2024–2025. The NDA 1 2024 maths split, for example, was about 18 algebra, 10 matrices, 11 trigonometry, 15 analytical geometry, 22 calculus with DE, 5 vectors and 19 statistics & probability, and NDA 2 2025 again stressed calculus and trigonometry. 2026 is covered from memory-based analyses and the writer's own knowledge; full analysis pages could not be fetched, and WebSearch returned only summaries. Patterns are described in our own words.

archetypes.pattern: Complex numbers: powers of i, cube roots of unity ω, modulus/argument or simplifying a quotient; distractors are ±1, ±i or ω/ω².
Quadratic equations: symmetric functions of roots (α+β, αβ, α³+β³, 1/α+1/β) or the condition for equal/real roots; trap is a sign error.
Sequences and series: nth term or sum of AP/GP/HP from two given terms; distractors from wrong index.
Permutations and combinations: arrangements of letters with repetition, digit-formation with divisibility, selections.
Binomial theorem: middle term, coefficient of x^k or term independent of x.
Sets and relations: cardinality of unions/intersections, classifying a relation as reflexive/symmetric/transitive.
Logarithms and number bases: evaluate nested logs or convert between binary and decimal.
Determinant properties: |kA|, |adj A|, skew-symmetric/singular matrices, determinant value without full expansion.
Matrix algebra: products, A² − kA, inverse, symmetric/skew-symmetric parts, Cayley–Hamilton shortcuts.
Exact values and identities: compound/multiple angles, products like sin15°cos15°, tan75° − tan15°.
Quadrant signs, trigonometric equations and principal values of inverse functions (trap: value outside principal range).
Properties of triangles (cosine/sine rule) and heights & distances.
Straight lines: distance between parallel lines, angle between lines, slope/intercept conditions.
Conics: eccentricity, foci, latus rectum of parabola/ellipse/hyperbola, circle centre and radius.
3D geometry: direction cosines, distance of a point from a plane, angle between planes/lines.
Limits and continuity: standard limits (sin x/x, (1+a/x)^x, (e^x−1)/x) and value making a function continuous.
Derivatives: chain, parametric, implicit and logarithmic differentiation.
Applications: maxima/minima, increasing/decreasing intervals, slope of tangent.
Real functions: domain, range and composition of functions.
Definite integrals using properties (odd/even, King's property ∫f(a+b−x)).
Indefinite integrals of standard forms (1/(x²+a²), substitution, by parts).
Area bounded by curves (parabola–line, circle).
Differential equations: order and degree, integrating factor, solution of variable-separable/linear equations.
Dot and cross products: perpendicularity condition, projection, area of parallelogram/triangle, |a×b|² + (a·b)².
Classical probability with dice, coins and cards (union of events, 'at least one').
Conditional probability, independent events and Bayes' theorem with two bags/urns.
Measures of central tendency and dispersion: effect of scaling/shifting on mean and variance, variance of natural numbers.
Binomial distribution parameters from mean and variance; correlation and regression coefficients.
Synonym of a word used in a sentence context; distractors include a look-alike word and an antonym.
Antonym of a word used in a sentence context; one distractor is a synonym.
Sentence split into parts (a)(b)(c) plus 'No error': subject–verb agreement traps (neither–nor, 'one of', collective nouns).
Spotting errors in prepositions, idiomatic usage, degrees of comparison or tense.
Replace the bold/underlined part (conditionals, 'senior to', subjunctive) or choose 'No improvement'.
Preposition, phrasal verb or conjunction blank in a single sentence.
Vocabulary blank: pick the contextually apt word from near-synonyms.
Arrange parts P, Q, R, S into a meaningful sentence; options are four permutations.
Short passage with a factual/inference question answered from a specific sentence.
Passage with main-idea, author's purpose or tone question.
Cloze passage: choose the word for a numbered blank (collocation/meaning).
Numerical in mechanics (kinematics, kinetic energy, projectile height) solvable in one step.
Optics and waves phenomena (twinkling, rainbow, speed of sound in media).
Electricity and magnetism: resistors in series/parallel, fuse, household circuits.
Common names and formulas of compounds (baking soda, plaster of Paris) and gases in daily use.
Physical vs chemical change, rusting, acids–bases and properties of elements.
Human physiology, nutrition and diseases (vitamins, hormones, blood groups, pathogens).
Cell and plant biology (organelles, photosynthesis).
Freedom movement events and personalities (INA, Dandi March, NCM withdrawal).
Ancient and medieval rulers and their titles/achievements.
Battles and colonial expansion (Plassey, Buxar, Panipat) and adversaries.
Indian physical geography: rivers (rift valley, west-flowing), passes, straits, boundaries.
World geography and climatology (deserts, winds, ocean features).
Earth and solar system (perihelion, International Date Line, seasons).
Constitutional articles and parts (emergency provisions, Fundamental Rights, Supreme Commander).
Elections and offices: electoral college, qualifications and age limits.
Basic economic concepts: direct/indirect taxes, inflation terms, banking basics.
Defence training institutions, ranks and equivalent ranks across services.
Bilateral/multilateral military exercises and partner countries.
Indigenous defence platforms and missiles (BrahMos, INS Vikrant, Tejas): type and developer.

questions.question: If ω is a non-real cube root of unity, then the value of (1 + ω − ω²)(1 − ω + ω²) is:
questions.explanation: Since 1 + ω + ω² = 0: 1 + ω − ω² = −ω² − ω² = −2ω² and 1 − ω + ω² = −ω − ω = −2ω. Product = 4ω³ = 4.

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0, then α³ + β³ equals:
questions.explanation: α + β = 5 and αβ = 6, so α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β) = 125 − 90 = 35. Check: the roots are 2 and 3, and 8 + 27 = 35.

questions.question: How many distinct arrangements can be made using all the letters of the word DEFENCE?
questions.explanation: DEFENCE has 7 letters with E repeated 3 times, so the count is 7!/3! = 5040/6 = 840.

questions.question: The middle term in the binomial expansion of (x + 1/x)¹⁰ is:
questions.explanation: There are 11 terms, so the middle term is T₆ = ¹⁰C₅ · x⁵ · (1/x)⁵ = 252.

questions.question: If log₂(log₃ x) = 1, then x equals:
questions.explanation: log₃ x = 2¹ = 2, so x = 3² = 9.

questions.question: In an arithmetic progression, the 5th term is 11 and the 11th term is 23. The 20th term is:
questions.explanation: a + 4d = 11 and a + 10d = 23 give d = 2 and a = 3. T₂₀ = 3 + 19 × 2 = 41.

questions.question: If n(A) = 20, n(B) = 15 and n(A ∪ B) = 28, then n(A ∩ B) is:
If A = [[2, 3], [1, 4]], then det(adj A) equals:
questions.explanation: |A| = 8 − 3 = 5. For an n × n matrix, |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹, so with n = 2 the value is 5¹ = 5.

questions.question: If A is a square matrix of order 3 with |A| = 4, then |2A| equals:
questions.explanation: |kA| = kⁿ|A| for an n × n matrix, so |2A| = 2³ × 4 = 32.

questions.question: The value of sin 15° · cos 15° is:
questions.explanation: sin 15° cos 15° = ½ sin 30° = ½ × ½ = 1/4.

questions.question: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ lies in the third quadrant, then sin θ equals:
questions.explanation: With a 3-4-5 triangle, |sin θ| = 3/5. Sine is negative in the third quadrant, so sin θ = −3/5.

questions.question: The value of tan 1° · tan 2° · tan 3° · … · tan 89° is:
questions.explanation: Pair tan θ with tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, so each pair has product 1. The middle term, tan 45°, is also 1, so the whole product is 1.

questions.question: The distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y − 7 = 0 and 6x + 8y + 6 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: Write the second line as 3x + 4y + 3 = 0. Distance = |−7 − 3| / √(3² + 4²) = 10/5 = 2.

questions.question: The eccentricity of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1 is:
If a line makes angles α, β and γ with the positive x, y and z axes respectively, then sin²α + sin²β + sin²γ equals:
questions.explanation: cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1, so the sum of the sin² terms is 3 − 1 = 2.

questions.question: The value of lim(x→0) (1 − cos 2x)/x² is:
questions.explanation: 1 − cos 2x = 2 sin²x, so the limit is 2 · lim (sin x/x)² = 2.

questions.question: If y = xˣ (x > 0), then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: ln y = x ln x, so (1/y) dy/dx = ln x + 1 and dy/dx = xˣ(1 + ln x).

questions.question: The maximum value of sin x + cos x is:
questions.explanation: sin x + cos x = √2 sin(x + 45°), whose maximum is √2.

questions.question: The value of ∫₀^(π/2) sin²x dx is:
questions.explanation: sin²x = (1 − cos 2x)/2, so the integral is [x/2 − sin 2x/4] from 0 to π/2 = π/4.

questions.question: The area of the region bounded by the curves y = x² and y = x is:
questions.explanation: The curves meet at x = 0 and x = 1, and y = x lies above. Area = ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6 square unit.

questions.question: The order and degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx)⁴ + y = 0 are respectively:
questions.explanation: The highest derivative is d²y/dx², so the order is 2. That derivative appears to the power 3, so the degree is 3.

questions.question: For what value of λ are the vectors i + λj + 2k and 2i − j + k perpendicular?
questions.explanation: The dot product must be zero: 2 − λ + 2 = 0, so λ = 4.

questions.question: If |a| = 3 and |b| = 4, then |a × b|² + (a · b)² equals:
questions.explanation: |a × b|² + (a · b)² = |a|²|b|²(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 9 × 16 = 144 (Lagrange's identity).

questions.question: Two fair dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers is 9 is:
questions.explanation: The favourable outcomes are (3,6), (4,5), (5,4) and (6,3), so P = 4/36 = 1/9.

questions.question: The variance of the first 10 natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: The variance of 1, 2, …, n is (n² − 1)/12 = 99/12 = 8.25.

questions.question: If A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.4, then P(A ∪ B) is:
Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to AUDACIOUS.
questions.explanation: Audacious means daring or bold.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to METICULOUS.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, that is, painstaking.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to AMELIORATE.
questions.explanation: Ameliorate means to make better, so its opposite is worsen.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Neither the captain nor the soldiers (A) / was aware of (B) / the change in plan. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Soldiers' is plural, so part B should read 'were aware of'.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
He is one of the best cadet (A) / that the academy (B) / has ever produced. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'One of the best' takes a plural noun, so part A should read 'one of the best cadets'.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'If I was the commander, I would order a retreat.' (underlined: If I was)
questions.explanation: An unreal present condition takes the subjunctive 'were': 'If I were the commander, I would …'. 'Had been' would need 'would have ordered'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The troops were asked to refrain ______ firing until ordered.
questions.explanation: 'Refrain' is followed by 'from'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Hardly had the train left the station ______ the alarm was raised.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly/Scarcely … when' is the correct correlative. 'No sooner' pairs with 'than'.

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: is the key to
Q: Discipline
R: success
S: in any profession
questions.explanation: Q-P-R-S gives 'Discipline is the key to success in any profession.'

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'The monsoon is often called the true finance minister of India. Although agriculture's share in national output has declined, nearly half of the workforce still depends on farming, and much of the cultivated area lacks assured irrigation. A weak monsoon therefore depresses rural incomes, which in turn reduces the demand for industrial goods.'
According to the passage, why does a weak monsoon hurt industry?
options: Lower rural incomes reduce the demand for industrial goods
Agriculture's share in output has increased
Irrigation has expanded to all farmland
questions.explanation: The last sentence links a weak monsoon to lower rural incomes and hence lower demand for industrial goods. The other options are either not stated or contradict the passage.

questions.question: A body of mass 2 kg moves with a speed of 3 m/s. Its kinetic energy is:
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.

questions.question: The twinkling of stars is mainly due to:
questions.explanation: Starlight is refracted by turbulent air layers whose refractive index keeps changing, so the apparent position and brightness of a star flicker.

questions.question: Three resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
In which of the following media does sound travel fastest?
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids such as steel (about 5,000 m/s), slower in water (about 1,500 m/s) and air (about 340 m/s). It cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: The chemical name of baking soda is:
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate (sodium bicarbonate), NaHCO₃. Washing soda is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.question: Which gas is commonly filled in incandescent electric bulbs to prolong the life of the filament?
questions.explanation: An inert gas such as argon (often mixed with nitrogen) slows evaporation of the tungsten filament and does not react with it.

questions.question: Rusting of iron requires the presence of:
questions.explanation: Rust (hydrated iron(III) oxide) forms only when both oxygen and water are present.

questions.question: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet-B light converts 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin into vitamin D₃.

questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor (for red cell transfusion)?
questions.explanation: O-negative red cells carry no A, B or Rh(D) antigens, so they can be given to recipients of any group in an emergency.

questions.question: Insulin is secreted by:
questions.explanation: The beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin.

questions.question: Who proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) at Singapore in October 1943?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Azad Hind provisional government in Singapore on 21 October 1943 and led the Indian National Army.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the English East India Company and:
questions.explanation: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, at Plassey in 1757.

questions.question: Who was the first and only Indian to hold the office of Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari succeeded Lord Mountbatten in June 1948 and held the post until it was abolished on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi undertake the Dandi March?
questions.explanation: The Dandi (Salt) March began from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and launched the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question: The Palk Strait separates India from:
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka.

questions.question: The boundary line between India and Pakistan demarcated in 1947 is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe. The McMahon Line concerns India–China and the Durand Line Afghanistan–Pakistan.

questions.question: The Western Ghats are also known as the:
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats are called the Sahyadri, especially in Maharashtra and Karnataka.

questions.question: The International Date Line roughly follows which meridian?
questions.explanation: The International Date Line broadly follows the 180° meridian, with deviations to avoid splitting land areas.

questions.question: Under the Constitution of India, the supreme command of the Defence Forces is vested in the:
questions.explanation: Article 53(2) vests the supreme command of the Defence Forces in the President.

questions.question: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 84 requires a Lok Sabha member to be at least 25 years old (30 for the Rajya Sabha).

questions.question: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Part III (Articles 12–35) covers Fundamental Rights. Part IV covers Directive Principles and Part IVA Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.explanation: A direct tax is paid by the person on whom it is levied, as with income tax. GST, customs and excise are indirect taxes.

questions.question: The Indian Military Academy, which trains officers for the Indian Army, is located at:
questions.explanation: IMA is at Dehradun. The NDA is at Khadakwasla (Pune), an OTA at Chennai and the Indian Naval Academy at Ezhimala.

questions.question: Which rank in the Indian Navy is equivalent to a Colonel in the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Colonel (Army) = Captain (Navy) = Group Captain (Air Force).

questions.question: If z = (1 + i)/(1 − i), then z¹⁰⁰ equals:
questions.explanation: (1 + i)/(1 − i) = (1 + i)²/2 = 2i/2 = i. Since i⁴ = 1 and 100 is a multiple of 4, i¹⁰⁰ = 1.

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0, then 1/α + 1/β equals:
The 3rd and 6th terms of a geometric progression are 12 and 96 respectively. The first term is:
questions.explanation: ar² = 12 and ar⁵ = 96, so r³ = 8 and r = 2. Then a × 4 = 12 gives a = 3.

questions.question: How many 4-digit numbers divisible by 5 can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
questions.explanation: The units digit must be 5 (0 is not available). The other three places are filled from the remaining 4 digits in 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 ways.

questions.question: The coefficient of x⁴ in the expansion of (1 + 2x)⁶ is:
questions.explanation: The term is ⁶C₄ (2x)⁴ = 15 × 16 x⁴ = 240x⁴.

questions.question: Let R = {(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2)} be a relation on the set {1, 2, 3}. Then R is:
options: Reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
Reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
questions.explanation: All (a, a) are present, so R is reflexive. (1, 2) is in R but (2, 1) is not, so it is not symmetric. Every chain such as (1, 1),(1, 2) or (1, 2),(2, 2) gives (1, 2), which is in R, so it is transitive.

questions.question: The binary number 101101 written in the decimal system is:
The value of the determinant of the matrix [[0, 2, −3], [−2, 0, 4], [3, −4, 0]] is:
questions.explanation: The matrix is skew-symmetric (Aᵀ = −A) and of odd order 3. Then |A| = |Aᵀ| = |−A| = (−1)³|A|, so |A| = 0.

questions.question: If A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]], then A² − 5A equals (I is the 2 × 2 identity matrix):
questions.explanation: A² = [[7, 10], [15, 22]] and 5A = [[5, 10], [15, 20]], so A² − 5A = [[2, 0], [0, 2]] = 2I. (This also follows from the Cayley–Hamilton theorem, since A² − 5A − 2I = 0.)

questions.question: The value of tan 75° − tan 15° is:
questions.explanation: tan 75° = 2 + √3 and tan 15° = 2 − √3, so the difference is 2√3.

questions.question: The principal value of sin⁻¹(sin 2π/3) is:
questions.explanation: sin 2π/3 = √3/2. The principal range of sin⁻¹ is [−π/2, π/2], and the angle there with sine √3/2 is π/3. 2π/3 lies outside the range.

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, a = 3, b = 5 and c = 7. The angle C is:
The acute angle between the lines y = √3x + 5 and √3y = x + 2 is:
questions.explanation: The slopes are √3 (inclination 60°) and 1/√3 (inclination 30°), so the angle between the lines is 30°.

questions.question: The eccentricity of the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: e² = 1 + b²/a² = 1 + 9/16 = 25/16, so e = 5/4. (4/5 is the reciprocal, a common slip.)

questions.question: The distance of the point (1, 2, 3) from the plane 2x − y + 2z + 4 = 0 is:
The value of lim(x→∞) (1 + 2/x)ˣ is:
questions.explanation: lim(x→∞) (1 + a/x)ˣ = eᵃ; here a = 2, so the limit is e².

questions.question: If x = a cos θ and y = a sin θ, then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: dx/dθ = −a sin θ and dy/dθ = a cos θ, so dy/dx = a cos θ/(−a sin θ) = −cot θ.

questions.question: The function f(x) = x³ − 3x has a local maximum at:
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 gives x = ±1. f″(x) = 6x is negative at x = −1, so there is a local maximum there (x = 1 gives a local minimum).

questions.question: The value of ∫₀^(π/2) sin x/(sin x + cos x) dx is:
questions.explanation: Call it I. Replacing x by π/2 − x gives I = ∫₀^(π/2) cos x/(cos x + sin x) dx. Adding, 2I = ∫₀^(π/2) 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.

questions.question: ∫ dx/(x² + 4) equals:
questions.explanation: ∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a) + C with a = 2.

questions.question: The integrating factor of the differential equation dy/dx + y/x = x² (x > 0) is:
questions.explanation: IF = e^(∫(1/x)dx) = e^(log x) = x.

questions.question: The area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are a = i + j and b = i − j + k is:
A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that it is a king or a heart is:
questions.explanation: P = (4 + 13 − 1)/52 = 16/52 = 4/13. The king of hearts must not be counted twice (that error gives 17/52).

questions.question: Bag I contains 3 red and 2 black balls; Bag II contains 2 red and 3 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn from it is red. The probability that it came from Bag I is:
questions.explanation: P(red) = ½ × 3/5 + ½ × 2/5 = ½. By Bayes' theorem, P(Bag I | red) = (½ × 3/5)/(½) = 3/5.

questions.question: The variance of a set of observations is 4. If each observation is multiplied by 3, the new variance is:
questions.explanation: Multiplying every observation by k multiplies the variance by k², so the new variance is 9 × 4 = 36.

questions.question: For a binomial distribution, the mean is 4 and the variance is 3. The number of trials n is:
questions.explanation: np = 4 and npq = 3 give q = 3/4 and p = 1/4, so n = 4/(1/4) = 16.

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to the word in capitals:
Given the bad weather, postponing the exercise was a PRUDENT decision.
questions.explanation: Prudent means showing good judgement and care for the future, i.e. wise.

questions.question:
Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals:
The spokesperson's reply was deliberately AMBIGUOUS.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; its opposite is clear. 'Vague' is a near-synonym.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The quality of the rations (A) / supplied to the troops (B) / have improved considerably. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the quality' (singular), not 'rations', so part C should read 'has improved considerably'.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
He did not know (A) / how to cope up (B) / with the sudden pressure. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'cope with', not 'cope up with'. The error is in part B.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'He is senior than me in service.' (underlined: senior than me)
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than': 'senior to me'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The cadets were warned to abide ______ the rules of the academy.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb is 'abide by', meaning to comply with.

questions.question:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: before the monsoon
Q: The engineers
R: completed the bridge
S: that connects the two villages
questions.explanation: Q-R-S-P gives 'The engineers completed the bridge that connects the two villages before the monsoon.' In QRPS the clause 'that connects the two villages' would wrongly describe the monsoon.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Himalayan glaciers feed rivers that sustain hundreds of millions of people downstream. In recent decades many of these glaciers have been thinning and retreating, largely because of rising temperatures. In the short run, faster melting can actually increase the flow in some rivers during summer. Over a longer period, however, as the ice reserves shrink, the same rivers may carry less water in the dry months, precisely when farmers and cities need it most. Scientists therefore argue that planning for water storage and efficient use must begin now, while the rivers are still full.'
According to the passage, why can the present increase in summer river flow be misleading?
options: It shows that the glaciers are growing
It is caused mainly by heavier monsoon rain
It comes from shrinking ice reserves and may be followed by lower dry-season flows
It proves that storing water is unnecessary
questions.explanation: The passage says faster melting raises flow only in the short run; as the ice shrinks, the rivers may carry less water in the dry months.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Himalayan glaciers feed rivers that sustain hundreds of millions of people downstream. In recent decades many of these glaciers have been thinning and retreating, largely because of rising temperatures. In the short run, faster melting can actually increase the flow in some rivers during summer. Over a longer period, however, as the ice reserves shrink, the same rivers may carry less water in the dry months, precisely when farmers and cities need it most. Scientists therefore argue that planning for water storage and efficient use must begin now, while the rivers are still full.'
The main purpose of the passage is to:
options: describe the beauty of Himalayan rivers
argue that the glaciers will never melt completely
urge early planning for water scarcity caused by glacier loss
questions.explanation: The passage builds up to its last sentence: planning for storage and efficient use must begin now.

questions.question:
In the following passage, choose the most appropriate word for the blank.
'Regular exercise not only strengthens the body but also ______ the mind, helping soldiers stay calm and alert under pressure.'
questions.explanation: The 'not only … but also' structure and 'helping soldiers stay calm and alert' need a positive verb: sharpens.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the maximum height it reaches is:
questions.explanation: h = u²/2g = 400/20 = 20 m. Forgetting the factor 2 gives 40 m.

questions.question: A rainbow is formed due to:
options: Diffraction of sunlight by dust particles
Refraction, dispersion and internal reflection of sunlight in raindrops
Interference of sunlight reflected from the ground
questions.explanation: Sunlight is refracted and dispersed on entering a raindrop, reflected inside it and refracted again on leaving, which separates the colours.

questions.question: A fuse wire used in household circuits should have:
options: Low resistance and high melting point
High resistance and high melting point
Low resistance and low melting point
High resistance and low melting point
questions.explanation: The fuse must heat up and melt quickly when excess current flows, so it is made of a high-resistance, low-melting-point alloy.

questions.question: The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is:
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O. CaSO₄·2H₂O is gypsum.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Melting changes only the state of water; no new substance forms. The others produce new substances.

questions.question: Which one of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Measles is caused by the measles virus. Typhoid, cholera and tuberculosis are bacterial diseases.

questions.question: In green plants, photosynthesis takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis. Mitochondria carry out respiration.

questions.question: Which incident led Mahatma Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.explanation: After a mob burnt a police station at Chauri Chaura in February 1922, Gandhi withdrew the movement.

questions.question: Who commanded the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the Indian National Army?
questions.explanation: Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (later Sahgal) led the INA's women's regiment. Usha Mehta ran the Congress Radio during Quit India.

questions.question: Which Gupta ruler was described by the historian V.A. Smith as the 'Napoleon of India'?
questions.explanation: Smith gave this title to Samudragupta because of his extensive military campaigns recorded in the Prayag Prashasti.

questions.question: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and:
questions.explanation: The Marathas were defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) in 1761. Babur and Ibrahim Lodi fought the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?
questions.explanation: The Narmada (like the Tapi) flows westward through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. The others are east-flowing.

questions.question: The Zoji La pass connects:
questions.explanation: Zoji La on the Srinagar–Leh highway links the Kashmir Valley with Ladakh.

questions.question: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert. Antarctica is larger, but it is a cold desert.

questions.question: The Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion) in:
questions.explanation: Perihelion falls around 3 January; aphelion around 4 July. This shows that seasons are caused by the tilt of the axis, not by distance from the Sun.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India can the President declare a National Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 352 deals with National Emergency, Article 356 with President's Rule, Article 360 with Financial Emergency, and Article 368 with amendment.

questions.question: The Vice-President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:
options: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies
All members of both Houses of Parliament
Elected members of the Lok Sabha only
Members of the Rajya Sabha only
questions.explanation: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by members of both Houses, including nominated members. State legislators take part only in the presidential election.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an indirect tax?
questions.explanation: GST is levied on supplies and passed on to the consumer, so it is an indirect tax. The others are taxes on income and are direct taxes.

questions.question: A situation of rising prices combined with stagnant output and high unemployment is called:
questions.explanation: Stagflation combines stagnation and inflation. Disinflation is a slowdown in the rate of inflation; deflation is a fall in the price level.

questions.question: The National Defence Academy is located at:
questions.explanation: NDA is at Khadakwasla near Pune. Dehradun has the IMA, Ezhimala the Indian Naval Academy and Dundigal the Air Force Academy.

questions.question: Which rank in the Indian Air Force is equivalent to a Major in the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Major = Squadron Leader = Lieutenant Commander. Flight Lieutenant equals Captain, and Wing Commander equals Lieutenant Colonel.

questions.question: BrahMos is a:
options: Intercontinental ballistic missile developed by DRDO alone
Supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia
questions.explanation: BrahMos, named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers, is a supersonic cruise missile built by the India–Russia joint venture BrahMos Aerospace.

questions.question: 'Yudh Abhyas' is a joint military exercise between India and:
questions.explanation: Yudh Abhyas is the India–US Army exercise. With Russia it is INDRA, with France Shakti and with Japan Dharma Guardian.

questions.question: India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier is:
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant, built at Cochin Shipyard, was commissioned in September 2022. Vikramaditya was bought from Russia, Viraat was ex-British, and Arihant is a nuclear submarine.
